assemblySteps.title: Lay the kit out and lift the tricap off the bowl
assemblySteps.summary: The kit arrives as the bowl with the main plate inside it, the tricap with its speaker and the six armed motors loose on top. Nothing goes in yet: the kit is laid out. Conflict, speaker screws: Beta calls out 2 / the mesh has 3 lugs / renders show 3 heads in a triangle round the ring. Taken: 2, third lug empty. Why: B19 and W0756 show two heads and a bare third lug (OS§4). Sources: G1, B19, W0756.

assemblySteps.title: Stick the five pads under the foot
assemblySteps.summary: The pads are K7's foot_pad_1 to 5; their adhesive backing is not a fastener the engine can name. Conflict, where the fifth pad goes: onto the rectangle outline / the recess beside the back plate. Taken: the recess beside the back plate. Why: the re-read follows the dotted line to the rim recess; the rectangle is a label recess (44 x 56 x 0.15). Sources: G2, S-6853, Mesh.

assemblySteps.title: Slip the sleeve over the USB extension
assemblySteps.summary: The sleeve sits some way along the cable, not against the panel socket. Not in the model: the sleeve, and a waypoint for it on the USB cable. The step names nothing. Sources: G3, S-6857, S-6789.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the USB socket into the foot and coil the cable once
assemblySteps.summary: Socket body lies flat on the floor inside the back plate, running forward. USB end a is the cable's own panel socket (K7's usb_socket). The turn is waypoint collar; no waypoint stands for the run along the floor. Conflict, countersinks at the two M3 holes: guide draws recesses for the heads / Pollen's v1.13.0 mesh (and our foot) has plain D3.47 holes / real frame W0373 shows sunk heads. Taken: countersunk holes. Why: the screws are countersunk and the real foot sinks them; owner decision 6 owes them in M4. Sources: G4, Mesh, W0373, S-6789.

assemblySteps.title: Drop the Power Board into the foot
assemblySteps.summary: The connector tail toward the back plate; the push button's cap out through the back plate's D6.98 hole, the jack's mouth at the D7.98 hole; the USB sleeve where the cable crosses the tail's left edge. The key cap (K7) rides in on the switch's plunger [I]: no step of the guide fits it. Conflict, which part is the 'longest tab': the right side tab / the connector tail. Taken: the connector tail. Why: the side tabs are mirror images; only the tail is longer. Sources: G5, ER.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the Power Board down
assemblySteps.summary: Sources: G6, Mesh.

assemblySteps.title: Stick the battery on the board and plug it into BAT
assemblySteps.summary: Pack long axis along y, centred about (6, 0), tape side down. BAT end a is the pack's own lead, so it is plugged as the pack goes in. The tape is not a fastener the engine can name. Conflict, battery wires: renders draw 3 / datasheet, Seeed's 4-pin note and real frame W0209 show 4. Taken: 4 wires, XT30(2+2). Why: printed sources and a real photo agree; the renders simplify. Conflict, the plug's path through the foot's inner wall: guide: low wall where the plug crosses (y -4..-25) / Pollen's mesh and our foot: full height at azimuth -21..0. Taken: the guide. Why: the plug cannot seat otherwise; owner decision 6 lowers the wall in M4. Sources: G7, BC, S-6795, W0209, Mesh.

assemblySteps.title: Plug the power and three motor cables into the Power Board
assemblySteps.summary: Each 3-way plug goes in with its contact window facing out; the blank face toward you is wrong; the two 200 mm cables may go in either of B and C; the low white 2-way part stays empty. Conflict, which white header is B: not lettered in the guide's view / Pollen's render prints B on the inner header. Taken: B inner, C outer. Why: the render's letter; C by elimination. Sources: G8, ER, W0209.

assemblySteps.title: Lower the Bottom Assembly onto the foot with every cable up the middle
assemblySteps.summary: The Power Board's silk arrow lines up with the arrow under the Bottom Assembly (the three screws allow three positions; the arrows pick one); press down gently. No waypoint stands for the central well on USB, PWR, C3 or C4; C1's guide clip is its waypoint guide_clip. Conflict, what the 100 mm cable's guide hole is: a hole through the bowl or plate / a clip on the main plate's yaw-servo cradle. Taken: the main plate's C-shaped clip over the servo's top end. Why: the step's zoom shows a curved strap rising from the well floor round one end of the yaw servo with the three wires inside; our main plate already draws such a clip. Sources: G9, G11, Mesh.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the foot to the turning ring from below
assemblySteps.summary: Turn the robot over. Sources: G10, B9, Mesh.

assemblySteps.title: Plug both cables into the yaw servo
assemblySteps.summary: Contact window facing out. No waypoint stands for the boss end or the way back up out of the well. Sources: G11, MD.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the link rods onto the motor arms
assemblySteps.summary: The screw enters from the ball's spherical side, the short collar faces the arm. Worked on the six armed motors (PB3) before they are seated. The rods arrive with both balls; v10 draws each arm's ball as its own part, lower_ball_1 to 6. Sources: G12, S-6801, S-6855, Mesh.

assemblySteps.title: Join motors 1 and 2 with a 40 mm cable
assemblySteps.summary: The two ports that face each other where the cases meet. No hard prerequisite; done outside the bowl for access. Sources: G13.

assemblySteps.title: Join motors 2 and 3 with a 200 mm cable
assemblySteps.summary: Motor 2's free side port to motor 3's outer port. Sources: G14.

assemblySteps.title: Join motors 4 and 5 with a 200 mm cable
assemblySteps.summary: Sources: G15.

assemblySteps.title: Join motors 5 and 6 with a 40 mm cable
assemblySteps.summary: The facing ports where the cases meet. Sources: G16.

assemblySteps.title: Seat the six motors in their numbered pockets
assemblySteps.summary: Pair 1-2 front-left, 3-4 at the back, 5-6 front-right (the URDF azimuths +44.74, +75.26, +164.74, -164.74, -75.26, -44.74); horn side toward the yaw axis, round boss toward the bowl wall; no fastener. Sources: G17.

assemblySteps.title: Press the side motor cables into the bowl's clips
assemblySteps.summary: Press the wires in one at a time. Conflict, 'three cables' between each tab pair: three separate cables / the three wires of the one cable that runs on that side. Taken: the three wires of C5 (left) or C7 (right). Why: no other cable runs along the bowl sides, and the caption asks for one-at-a-time pressing [I]. Sources: G18.

assemblySteps.title: Rest the tricap on the motors without screws
assemblySteps.summary: Check the engraved numbers: pods 1-2 front-left, 3-4 back, 5-6 front-right. SPK end a is the speaker's own lead, soldered in the kit: plugged as the tricap goes in. Sources: G19.

assemblySteps.title: Thread the two 200 mm cables through loop C and under arch B
assemblySteps.summary: Loop A stays empty for now. Sources: G20.

assemblySteps.title: Plug the two 200 mm cables into motors 3 and 4
assemblySteps.summary: The two inner ports at the middle of pod 3-4's back face; the two cables are interchangeable; the motors may be lifted a little for access. Conflict, a cable from motor 3 to motor 4: the step's title names one / caption and picture give each motor its own cable from the board. Taken: no 3-4 cable. Why: the caption and the picture agree; G15 warns 3 and 4 stay apart. Sources: G21.

assemblySteps.title: Thread the head-bound cables through loop A and arch B
assemblySteps.summary: Above B, outer to inner: USB, power, C2. SPK's lead_end is where its lead leaves the can's stub. Sources: G22.

assemblySteps.title: Turn the body end to end and check nothing catches
assemblySteps.summary: The pose sweeps yaw_body from -160 to +160 deg; which end first is not stated. Conflict, how the strand is drawn: step 22: one strand through A then B / step 23: two strands, power making a U-turn round loop A's side. Taken: through A, then B. Why: step 22's caption states it; step 23 only checks rotation. Sources: G23.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the tricap to the main plate
assemblySteps.summary: Sources: G24.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the Bottom Head onto the six upper ball ends
assemblySteps.summary: Arrows aligned; each slot number matched to its motor number. Conflict, nuts for these screws: the callout lists none / the traps are drawn with nuts / S-6800: the part ships with six nuts. Taken: nuts pre-embedded (PB5). Why: the shop page and the trap drawing agree. Sources: G25, S-6800.

assemblySteps.title: Lead the neck cables up through the head part
assemblySteps.summary: Conflict, which hole: the central D18.93 bore / the C-shaped chimney behind the fan bay. Taken: the chimney. Why: the bore is the fan's air hole under the 20 x 20 bay; the bundle is drawn passing behind it (finding 1). Sources: G26, Mesh.

assemblySteps.title: Feed the fan lead and Wi-Fi coax up through the head board's window
assemblySteps.summary: Not in the model: the CM4, the heat sink and spacers, the Wi-Fi patch and its coax (held out). FAN end a is the fan's own lead, plugged as it arrives. Conflict, where the fan is held: product.json seats it in the head part's bay (fan_in_bay) / the guide's renders hang it under the heat sink, arriving with the board. Taken: it travels with the board. Why: CR and G27 show it under the heat sink, its bottom 1.7 above the bay's floor [I]; the fan's own fixing is not shown. Sources: G27, CR.

assemblySteps.title: Camera cable at J (done in the kit; for reference)
assemblySteps.summary: Both side latches closed. Done in the kit; plugged here so the sequence states it. Our head board's J8 is a bottom-contact socket (AFC07-S22FCC-00), so the camera cable goes in with its contacts down, toward the board. Inserted contacts up, as the guide shows on Pollen's own board, it touches nothing: nothing shorts, but the camera is not found. Between J8 and the camera the cable then takes one extra half twist along its length, or its fold reversed; it has about 114 mm to spare. The camera end (15-way, step 48) is unchanged: contacts down, toward the camera's board. Conflict, which board the step shows: the inset photos / the step-30 photo and render. Taken: the step-30 board: J 22-way at 0.5 mm. Why: the insets show another board (a Lite CSI bridge), and the video's board has a 15-way J with the cable in I (OS finding 2). This departs from the guide on purpose, decided 2026-11-08: the board stays as it is and the insertion changes. Sources: G28, PP, SP, W2503, j8-camera.

assemblySteps.title: Pass every neck cable up through the board's window
assemblySteps.summary: Sources: G29.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the head board onto the head part's posts
assemblySteps.summary: Leave the four gold-ringed outer holes (heat sink) and the CM4's four alone. Conflict, what the four posts carry: our neck_reference labels them for the shells / the guide screws the board to them. Taken: the head board. Why: four fits of photos to the posts agree to 0.13 mm. Sources: G30, SB.

assemblySteps.title: Drop the top shell over the neck
assemblySteps.summary: Its back toward motors 3-4. The guide fits it once the head part and board are on. Sources: G31.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the top shell from below
assemblySteps.summary: Turn the body over. Conflict, how far the screw tip stands out: G31's render: about 3 mm / the mesh's 2 mm cap: about 6 mm. Taken: unresolved. Why: only a real part settles it. Sources: G32, Mesh.

assemblySteps.title: Set the two lenses in the glasses holder
assemblySteps.summary: Convex side down; the Ø40 lens is the big one (right eye), Ø30 the small. Sources: G33.

assemblySteps.title: Put the fisheye lenses in their caps
assemblySteps.summary: Each lens goes in from the cap's hollow side. At the bench: both caps with their fisheyes are one unit, which step 35 snaps on. Sources: G34, S-6797.

assemblySteps.title: Snap the lens caps onto the holder
assemblySteps.summary: From the holder's back; three clips on each cap meet three windows. Sources: G35.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the glasses holder into the front shell
assemblySteps.summary: Two holder holes stay empty: they took the beta camera carrier. The front head is built at the bench and goes onto the robot in step 48. Sources: G36.

assemblySteps.title: Slide each antenna motor into its case
assemblySteps.summary: R motor into the R case, L into L; the servo's rear end goes in, the interface stays outside; line up the case's circular mark (not identified in the picture). The back shell's unit is built at the bench, steps 37 to 39, and slid on in step 40. No fastener. Sources: G37.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the antenna cases into the back shell
assemblySteps.summary: R case on the shell's R mark, L on L. Sources: G38.

assemblySteps.title: Chain the antenna motors
assemblySteps.summary: The left motor's window port stays empty. No waypoint stands for C10's loose S or the U-tab C9 lies over. Conflict, which catalog port is notch-side: the guide names ports by place only. Taken: right port_b and left port_a. Why: the only pairing that leaves the 100 mm cable slack: 72.3 mm straight, the other pair 100.1 [I computed]. Sources: G39.

assemblySteps.title: Slide the back shell onto the head part
assemblySteps.summary: From behind, along the head part's rails. Conflict, how the head shells mate: product.json: back_on_front (back shell screwed to the front shell's upper corner boss), front_on_head (front shell's chin pad on the head part's tray) / guide: back shell slides on the head part's rails and is screwed from below (41); front shell screwed to the back from behind (49). Taken: the guide. Why: it is the production order; the doc's relations place the parts correctly but name other carriers. Sources: G40.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the back shell to the head part from below
assemblySteps.summary: Conflict, slits per ladder beside the screws: 8 (first count) / 9 (second count and the mesh). Taken: 9. Why: counted twice and sliced on the mesh. Sources: G41.

assemblySteps.title: Clamp the USB cable under the Cable Holder with the head raised
assemblySteps.summary: Not in the model: the Cable Holder; the clamp is USB's waypoint cable_holder on the back shell. No pose: no source gives the six neck angles of the head at its highest. Sources: G42, MD, UC.

assemblySteps.title: Plug in the speaker, the fan and both motor cables
assemblySteps.summary: C9 is W2's 100 mm cable for the guide's 40 mm; its spare lies loose by E (waypoint spare). No waypoint stands for the arcs from the window. Conflict, whether 40 mm reaches from E to the right antenna motor: guide: the 40 mm cable runs straight up from E to the motor's window port / our model: 38.8 mm straight between the two plug exits, so no slack. Taken: flagged, not resolved. Why: E's position, the motor's pose or Seeed's length convention is off by a few mm; nothing read settles which. Sources: G43.

assemblySteps.title: Plug in the power cable and the USB extension
assemblySteps.summary: No waypoint stands for the run from the holder down to H. Sources: G44.

assemblySteps.title: Stick the Wi-Fi patch inside the back shell
assemblySteps.summary: Long side vertical. Not in the model: the patch antenna, its adhesive and its coax (held out). The step names nothing. Sources: G45.

assemblySteps.title: Slide the top head (mic) assembly onto the back shell
assemblySteps.summary: Along the two rails on the back shell's top edge, into its notches; no screw. The mic cable arrives plugged at the strip (PB8): end a is plugged here, through the bar's slot. Conflict, what carries the mic cover: product.json: mic_on_front / guide: the back shell's top rails. Taken: the back shell. Why: the guide's slide arrows and notches. Sources: G46.

assemblySteps.title: Plug the mic flat cable into K
assemblySteps.summary: Lift the flip latch; blue side up, or the printed 'Main Board' side up on the black cable; close the latch. Conflict, cable length: 150 mm (Pollen's how-to) / 15 mm (FAQ). Taken: 150 mm. Why: 15 mm cannot reach K; the how-to and the suggested Molex part agree. Sources: G47, change_mic_fpc_cable.md, #1119.

assemblySteps.title: Plug the camera cable into the camera
assemblySteps.summary: Hold the front head close; open the latch, contacts down, push in, close both side latches. The front head comes in here, held close; step 49 screws it. CAM's half twist is decision 25's. Sources: G48.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the front shell to the back shell from behind
assemblySteps.summary: Conflict, front shell carrier: product.json: front_on_head (chin pad on the tray) / guide: screwed to the back shell. Taken: the guide. Why: four screws into the back shell are the only fixing drawn. Sources: G49.

assemblySteps.title: Screw the antennas onto their interfaces
assemblySteps.summary: The body keys on the interface's flat. Conflict, interface-to-horn screws (fitted in the kit): PDF prints 2.5x6 / the horn's holes are D1.6, and B7 and ROBOTIS use M2 tapping screws there. Taken: open. Why: no picture settles it. Sources: G50, PDF, S-6803.

assemblySteps.title: Verify regulated servo rail before powering on
assemblySteps.summary: Confirm the servo bus is regulated to 5.0 V (within the 3.7–6.0 V ROBOTIS XL330/XC330 rating) before powering on.
